headline: A short extension keeps DEA's temporary schedule I control on fentanyl-related substances in place until September 30, 2021.
what_it_does: The DEA had placed fentanyl-related substances in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act on a temporary basis. That order was set to expire on May 6, 2021. This law extends the order until September 30, 2021, so the same federal drug rules keep applying during that period.

who_it_affects.group: People who make, sell, or possess fentanyl-related substances
who_it_affects.how: The federal schedule I rules that apply to these substances stay in effect through September 30, 2021.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers and laboratories that handle these substances
who_it_affects.how: They continue to work under schedule I federal controls, which limit how the substances can be stored, used, and shared.
The DEA keeps its temporary scheduling authority over these substances without a gap after May 6, 2021.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted May 4, 2021, and the extended order runs through September 30, 2021.
